question: Can a regularized runner-level market-offset residual using only frozen Candidate-A/B1a winner outputs improve on the market winner baseline?

market_baseline_construction.operation: normalize inverse odds within 3rentan then marginalize normalized ticket mass by first-place car
market_baseline_construction.live_transport_status: NOT_ESTABLISHED; historical closing-price use is diagnostic only
market_baseline_construction.future_requirement: replace with a preregistered decision-time PRE market snapshot if prospective source semantics are approved

residual_features: candidate_a market-ratio x centered log-market interaction
b1a market-ratio x centered log-market interaction
R1_model.objective: race-normalized multinomial log loss plus L2 penalty

interpretation: A-only rolling CV produced a small probability improvement, but it did not transport to burned B on the primary log-loss metric.
The 0.2 percentage-point B top1 accuracy increase is too small and conflicts with slightly worse B log loss; it is not an adoption signal.
Existing Candidate-A/B1a winner outputs alone do not provide a robust residual layer over the market baseline.
The next safe development step is to test a strongly regularized market-offset residual using raw point-in-time PRE runner and race context features, still on burned A+B only.
No economic optimization should be performed until probability metrics improve over market-only out of chronological development blocks.
next_safe_tasks: construct runner-level PRE residual feature matrix with strict allowlist
forward burned-B diagnostic comparison to market-only
